claim.statement: On 1 May 2026, Taadol/TradeNews reported Farvardin 1405 Center of Statistics data showing that food inflation remained centered on basic goods: total point-to-point inflation was 73.5%, food/beverages were 115.4%, oils/fats 233.6%, red and white meat 140.9%, bread/cereals 138.9%, and dairy 127.3%; annual food/beverage inflation was 74.9% versus total annual inflation of 53.7%, with bread/cereals annual inflation at 106.7%.
claim.subject: Iran Farvardin 1405 food inflation
claim.object: basic-goods inflation far above total inflation

evidence.summary: Taadol/TradeNews summarized Farvardin 1405 Center of Statistics food inflation by category, including total, food/beverage, oils/fats, meat, bread/cereals, dairy, monthly, and annual readings.

information_depth.rationale: The article gives specific Center-of-Statistics figures across point-to-point, monthly, and annual categories.

assessment.uncertainty: The row relies on media reporting of official statistics rather than a direct SCI table; retrieve the original statistical bulletin if it becomes available.

claim.statement: By 26 April 2026, Iranian support messaging had moved toward a staged cash-and-credit bridge: KhabarOnline/EghtesadOnline said support-institution pensions would be paid on 20 Ordibehesht, deciles 1-3 would receive 400,000 toman per person on 25 Ordibehesht, deciles 4-9 would receive 300,000 toman per person on 31 Ordibehesht, and household heads could activate Tara credit up to twice their monthly subsidy for 12 goods categories at 17,000 online/offline stores, with repayment beginning 30 days after purchase and unpaid debt deducted from the next subsidy.
claim.subject: Iran Ordibehesht 1405 household support system
claim.object: staged cash payments plus subsidy-backed consumer credit

evidence.summary: KhabarOnline/EghtesadOnline listed payment dates and amounts for support pensions and subsidy deciles, plus Tara credit rules, store network, categories, repayment start, and next-subsidy deduction.

information_depth.rationale: The source provides dates, amounts, eligibility bands, credit ceiling, repayment rule, and deduction mechanism.

assessment.uncertainty: The article describes the policy offer, not redemption rates, store failures, debt stress, or household outcomes.

claim.statement: The v38 broader May 2 Persian xPool food/bread query emitted 117 items with 115 usable texts; manual coding found 22 bread-coded, 0 kalabarg-coded, 62 food-coded, 42 inflation/livelihood-coded, 8 queue/shortage-coded, and 5 protest-term texts, while manual reading found general inflation anger, household food-stress examples, bread-price chatter, anti-regime discourse, Dey 1404 worker-death memory, and one weak Ahvaz control-inflation slogan post, but no clean source-near bakery-line riot, bread protest, or kalabarg coordination cluster.
claim.subject: Persian X food and bread discourse on May 2
claim.object: food stress and inflation anger without a clean bread or kalabarg action cluster

evidence.summary: The saved xPool result completed 10 pages, emitted 117 items, and stopped at MAX_PAGES_REACHED for a broad May 2 Persian bread/food/inflation query.
The notes record manual coding of 115 usable texts and manual inspection showing broad food/inflation anger but no clean bread riot, bread protest, or kalabarg coordination cluster.

information_depth.rationale: The sample is useful for visible social discourse and bounded negative evidence, but xPool is not representative and may miss suppressed local action.

assessment.uncertainty: Local bakery videos, provincial bread notices, store-level kalabarg failures, or later payment-date complaints could quickly change this read.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v38 - food inflation hardens, bread stays politically contained
synthesis.summary: The thirty-eighth pass returns to the bread and food-subsidy question and does not find a clean bread-riot or kalabarg coordination cluster. That is containment, not relief. Existing v18 rows still hold: official bread messaging says no new price policy and treats increases as violations, while guild and citizen evidence says sangak/barbari prices are not matching official rates and bakery management satisfies neither customers nor bakers. The new hard update is Farvardin 1405 food inflation: Taadol/TradeNews reports Center-of-Statistics figures with total point inflation at 73.5%, food/beverages at 115.4%, oils/fats at 233.6%, meat at 140.9%, bread/cereals at 138.9%, and annual bread/cereal inflation at 106.7%. The policy response is also clearer: Ordibehesht support is staged through cash payments and Tara consumer credit, including credit up to twice the monthly subsidy and next-subsidy deduction for unpaid debt. The broader May 2 xPool sample shows food and inflation anger, household stress, and bread chatter, but no source-near bread action cluster. Net: bread is still politically quiet in visible evidence, but quiet is being bought with enforcement, subsidy scheduling, deferred decisions, and credit rather than restored affordability.
synthesis.limitations: The absence of a clean bread-action cluster is bounded by xPool and Exa visibility, blackout conditions, and source-near reporting constraints. The Tara/yaranah article describes policy design rather than uptake, store failures, debt deductions, or household outcomes. Follow 15, 20, 25, and 31 Ordibehesht for payment-date complaints, kalabarg redemption failures, provincial bread enforcement, and whether food pressure becomes explicit in worker, retiree, or bazaar action.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis combines fresh official-statistic reporting, a current subsidy-credit article, a completed xPool sample, and existing canonical bread/food rows.

operations.rationale: Farvardin food inflation above 115% raises the test for whether kalabarg or cash support can blunt food-pressure anger.
Triple-digit food-category inflation is a direct pathway from household squeeze to nutrition and health-access risk.
The support schedule and Tara credit mechanism are the concrete policy response to watch around the kalabarg and food-pressure question.
Subsidy-backed credit can delay household pressure but may also intensify later labor and retiree anger if deductions or store failures appear.
The May 2 social sample still shows bread and food pressure without clean visible bakery-line unrest.
The sample bounds current visible bread unrest while keeping the end-Khordad price-reform watch active.
The sample shows food and bread stress but not yet the bread-riot path implied by the rial-collapse question.
